record.question: What is the best reason for the nurse in instructing the patient to rotate injection sites for insulin?
options: Lipodystrophy can result and is extremely painful
Poor rotation technique can cause superficial hemorrhaging
Lipodystrophic areas can result, causing erratic insulin absorption rates from these
Injection sites can never be reused
record.explanation: Answer C: Lipodystrophic areas can result, causing erratic insulin absorption rates from these. Repeated injections in the same area can cause lipodystrophy, which may lead to erratic insulin absorption; systematic site rotation reduces this risk. Reference: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/insulin-medicines-treatments. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
